title: Caloric cooling devices and systems - Nature Energy
gist: Nature Energy review (abstract only available) benchmarks magnetocaloric, elastocaloric, electrocaloric and barocaloric cooling devices against vapour-compression and thermoelectric technologies, finding a persistent gap between material-level effects and device-level performance, and outlines a roadmap to commercial deployment.

insights.claim: Caloric cooling (magnetocaloric, elastocaloric, electrocaloric and barocaloric) is an emerging solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration with potential to eliminate high-global-warming-potential refrigerants.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A long-dated disruption option for HVAC and refrigeration incumbents facing refrigerant phase-downs.

insights.claim: Despite large caloric effects at the material level, a gap persists between intrinsic material performance and device-level operation, making efficient and scalable systems the main challenge.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Commercial timelines hinge on engineering (heat exchange, actuation, durability) rather than discovering new materials.

insights.claim: The review benchmarks efficiency, temperature span, cooling power density, durability and cost against vapour-compression and thermoelectric technologies.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives the metric set to judge any caloric-cooling startup's claims.

insights.claim: Fatigue-resistant shape memory alloys, multilayer electrocaloric architectures and natural rubber-based elastocaloric systems have improved durability, power density and cost-effectiveness of caloric devices.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: These three technical routes are the ones to watch for first commercial products.

insights.claim: The authors analyse system integration and cost trends and outline a roadmap to accelerate the transition to sustainable cooling technologies.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Cost-evolution projections in the full paper are the key diligence item; only the abstract is available here.
